narrative.title: Shunting the Print Queue to the Back of the Line
narrative.scenario: A print farm's job queue is a single chain, and every shift change the last k jobs are moved — in their existing order — to the front, so long-waiting jobs print first. A counter records the queue length while the tail is temporarily looped back to the head, which turns the chain into a ring: the shift then becomes a single cut at the right spot of that ring rather than k separate moves. Jobs past the cut become the new front, and the ring is cut open again.
narrative.inputFormat: An array head of n node values and an integer k, the number of right rotations (possibly larger than n).
narrative.outputFormat: The values of the list after rotating right by k places.

testCases.explanation: The last two jobs (4, 5) move to the front in order; the cut on the ring lands after node 3.
Four rotations on a length-3 queue collapse to one effective rotation via modulo.

hintLevels: Level 1: Rotating right by k just means the last k nodes lead — find where to cut after one walk, not k walks.
Level 2: Measure the length while looping the tail back to the head; the effective shift is k mod length.
Level 3: The new tail sits at position (len - k mod len - 1) from the old head; sever it, promote its next, and remember to break the ring you closed.
